name: Ötztaler Höhenstraße
kurzbeschreibung: The 83 km-long scenic road winds along the Ötztaler mountains, offering countless viewpoints, hiking trails, and mountain huts.
preis: Mautgebühr ca. 24–26 € pro PKW (mit Ötztal Summer Card kostenlos)
beschreibung:
Overview

The Ötztal Glacier Road (Ötztaler Gletscherstraße), ascending high above Sölden, represents an extraordinary feat of alpine road engineering and the undisputed highest paved road in the Eastern Alps. Spanning roughly 15 kilometers, this immaculate mountain thoroughfare conquers an incredible 1,460 vertical meters, climbing from Sölden (1,370 m) straight into the glacial domain of eternal ice. Switchbacking in soaring serpentines and rock galleries, the road initially reaches the Rettenbach Glacier terminal at 2,675 meters. From there, it threads through the 1.7-kilometer Rosi Mittermaier Tunnel—the highest motor-traffic tunnel in Europe at 2,829 meters—before culminating at the Tiefenbach Glacier at an astonishing 2,830 meters elevation. Framed by icy summits including the Wildspitze (3,770 m) and Weißkugel, this celestial landscape served in 2015 as the signature filming location for the James Bond blockbuster "Spectre", celebrated nearby by the architectural museum 007 ELEMENTS.

Route & Requirements

Driving the Glacier Road is a bucket-list expedition for motorists, motorbike tourers, and endurance road cyclists. The roadway is broad, fully paved, and protected by engineered safety barriers (toll fee approx. €24 to €26 per car; free with the Ötztal Summer Card). At the high-altitude glacier bases, accessible adventures beckon for all generations: at Tiefenbach Glacier, an engineered metal catwalk leads to the breathtaking Tiefenbachkogl Suspension Footbridge, cantilevered 25 meters out over sheer glacial ice (easy grade T1, family-friendly). Active mountain walkers can hike from Rettenbach Glacier along marked moraine routes to the Braunschweiger Hütte (2,759 m) or circle the glacial lake (approx. 1.5 to 2 hours, moderate grade T2). Drivers must utilize engine braking during descents to preserve brake systems. Sturdy footwear and warm windproof outer layers are mandatory at nearly 3,000 meters elevation even in July. Leashed dogs are permitted throughout the glacier area.

Visit & Arrival

Rail passengers travel via ÖBB mainline trains to Ötztal Bahnhof station, transferring to regional bus line 320 departing every thirty minutes to Sölden. During the summer hiking season, dedicated Ötztal glacier shuttle buses run directly from Sölden's village center up to the Rettenbach and Tiefenbach stations. Drivers navigate via the Inntal autobahn A12 (exit Ötztal) and follow highway B186 through the valley to Sölden, branching onto the glacier toll road just above town. Generous free parking is available at both glacier terminals. The road is accessible from early June through early November, weather permitting.

Tips

Step out onto the glass-and-steel catwalk of the Tiefenbachkogl Footbridge to gaze directly into the precipitous north ice walls of Mount Wildspitze (3,770 m). Stop at the contemporary Rettenbach Glacier Restaurant to sample hearty Tyrolean mountain herb soup and warm sweet yeast dumplings on the observation terrace.
